h: Making the Most of the North Bay
p: Getting to SEA LIFE Scarborough can be half the fun. The North Bay Railway, a miniature line, runs from near Peasholm Park up to Scalby Mills in the season, dropping you a short walk from the aquarium's pyramids. Little ones love it, and it saves tired legs on the way back too.

Inside, plan for a couple of hours, and check the day's talk and feeding times when you arrive so you can build your route around them. Younger children get a lot out of the touch-style displays and the creatures from the Yorkshire coast, because it connects to the rock pools and beaches they'll have been exploring all holiday.

The North Bay is the gentler end of town, and it rewards a slow afternoon. Peasholm Park sits nearby with its boating lake and pagoda, and the Open Air Theatre, which hosts big summer concerts, is tucked behind it. Down on the beach the sand is great for castles, and there's a long, flat promenade for scooters and buggies.

When you're ready for the busier side of Scarborough, the walk round Marine Drive beneath the headland takes you to the harbour and the South Bay. There you'll find the bright lights of the arcades and amusements, fish and chips by the harbour and plenty of seaside bustle. Do bear in mind that some amusement venues include adult gaming areas that are strictly 18+.
If you're staying a few days, Robin Hood's Bay and Whitby are both an easy drive up the coast, and the North York Moors are on the doorstep for walks and big skies.
